newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Russian premier slams British beef "criminals".
newsitem.headline: Russian premier slams British beef "criminals".

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin hit out on Friday at "criminals" who exported British beef to Russia despite a ban imposed because of a health scare.

"It's pure crime and should be seen as such and anyone who has been involved in this is a criminal and should be treated as such -- as a criminal," he told a news conference on the second day of an official visit to Brussels.

Russia said last week it had seized 730 tonnes of beef labelled as being Belgian but originating in Britain which is not allowed to export beef because of fears that so-called mad cow disease can be transmitted to humans.
He said the Belgian authorities had since taken "fairly radical steps" to crack down on the fraud.

The European Commission said earlier this month it had traced 1,600 tonnes of British beef that had been illegally exported to the Netherlands, Egypt and Russia either via Belgium or using Belgian certificates.
Chernomyrdin said Russia was stepping up controls around its borders.

European Commission President Jacques Santer told the news conference after meeting the Russian premier that both sides had agreed to set up an early warning system to ensure that it did not happen again.
About 170 tonnes of British beef have also been seized in the German port of Hamburg destined for Russia.
